title: Prove least denominator 12,480 for the A1 zero spectral projector (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Exact finite certificate with a scoped arithmetic obstruction, produced by Nick Petalas. The zero spectral projector of unpaidmoon's historical `A_1` joint `(+1,+1)` 216-dimensional block has least integral denominator **12,480 = 2^6 · 3 · 5 · 13**. Thus this exact filter cannot be implemented by a linear program using only dyadic coefficients in the pinned basis, including a polynomial in `A_1` with dyadic coefficients.

```text
pinned B = 4 A_1 and signed-orbit basis (#6964)
    -> explicit Q / 12480
    -> exact projector and whole-kernel completeness identities
    -> four reduced entries force denominator 12480
```

The new result is the explicit projector and its sharp denominator. No new kappa or selected-frontier change. Predecessor matrix and basis are cited inputs; predecessor spectral and nullity suites are not replayed.

## Evidence

Before, #6964 supplies the matrix, orbit basis and characteristic polynomial; the open nullity packages describe kernel dimensions. This package supplies every entry of the projector and a denominator lower bound.

The standard-library verifier checks every entry of `Q^2=12480 Q`, `MQ=QM=0`, `DM=M^T D`, and `DQ=Q^T D`. It computes `det(M+Q) mod 1000003 = 905182`, proving that the projector covers the entire kernel. Four reduced entries have denominator lcm 12480. It enumerates rank 24 and 4,608 nonzero numerator entries. Four false certificates are rejected, including a zero projector that passes annihilation and idempotence but fails completeness.

Locally passed at head `ad53e04a014de87eff166032901d7b6197419adf`: registered normal/optimized replay, both warning-strict direct commands, metadata/source pins, committed bytes and declared source-history preflight, in-memory syntax compilation, and diff whitespace checks. Each registered command was also timed directly, at 0.138 and 0.139 seconds, below its 120-second limit. Environment: CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only. The selected source-binding orientation also passes for selected #7000.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/a1-zero-projector-denominator/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B -O research/a1-zero-projector-denominator/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a1-zero-projector-denominator
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/a1-zero-projector-denominator --check-source-history
```

Other machines may substitute their CPython 3.12 path. Direct marker: `PASS_A1_ZERO_PROJECTOR_DENOMINATOR`. Registered marker: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Publication preflight passes all eleven package/input files. Exact source pins are in `SOURCES.json`, at canonical-main base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19571856). Credit unpaidmoon #6964 for the mathematical input; retain JoyboyBrian's decomposition handoff, the sign-stabilizer construction, aliromman's query/Bell-action lineage, krzysztofwojt's one-slot polynomial, petalas's earlier degree lower bound, and the doubled representation. The proof distinguishes these premises from the new result.

## Limitations

One exact historical block and its pinned coordinates. No exclusion of other invariant filters, rational programs with paid odd division, approximation, or nonlinear programs. No physical caller, native/restoration bill, compiler closure, selected cold replay, predecessor degree-216/881 replay, Lean or Docker run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Price a factored exact filter with legal odd division and full output restoration. The physical contract and complete paid/target invoice remain unresolved.
- Specify a useful alternative invariant filter and its actual consumer identity, then ask whether that different filter can be dyadic.

## Related open work

The open-PR corpus and live claims were checked; sparse local-note coverage is incomplete, supplemented by Git-tree README and merged-PR searches. No matching projector-denominator result was found. These papers/packages are cited without additional replays:

- #7018 computes the zero multiplicity on this exact matrix; its 24 agrees with the rank of this projector.
- #7064 computes a different eigenvalue's multiplicity on this matrix.
- #7066 computes zero multiplicities on the other joint sign spaces.
- #7008 splits this block by its signed normalizer.
- #7022 studies preservers outside that normalizer.
- #7023 computes the polynomial of its eight-dimensional isotypic summand.
- #7059 studies stabilizer movers of that isotypic summand.
- #7061 computes a polynomial on the eighty-dimensional isotypic summand.
- #7065 computes a polynomial on the other dihedral component; no multiplicity-space matrix is constructed here.
- #7019 studies different eight-dimensional joint spaces.
- #7071 constructs a transporter for those different joint spaces.
- #7009 splits moved sign characters of the same historical operator.
- #7036 computes a polynomial on a moved-character eigenspace.
- #7057 computes its zero multiplicity, on a different matrix.
- #7082 cuts that moved-character eigenspace by another invariant subspace.
- #7020 studies involutions in another sector of the historical operator.
- #7068 computes a polynomial on a subspace of that other sector.
- #7069 studies sign changes of a trace in that other sector.
- #7172 bounds the all-width Gram annihilator and stabilization; this PR does not extend its question or compute another width.
- #7467 by petalas constructs a dyadic multiplicity operator on a dihedral component of this historical A_1 block. Its operator denominator is a different quantity from the zero spectral projector denominator computed here; no new computation was run to compare them.

The closeout check read this account's open PRs created since the CLAIM: #7461, #7462, #7464, #7465, #7466 and #7467, in addition to this PR. Only #7467 studies this historical operator. The others concern quadratic-refinement widths, CNOT words, compiler plateau divisors, helper recharts and robust pairing capacity. No competing value for this projector denominator was found.
